Key_Finding: 24,918 incident-level records with 36 attributes; each incident number is unique
Implication: Suitable for incident-level EDA and later modelling

Key_Finding: No duplicate incident numbers and no exact duplicate rows were detected
Implication: No duplicate-removal action is required based on the current incident-level dataset

Key_Finding: Class 0 = 54.37% and Class 1 = 45.63%; no severe class imbalance
Implication: No immediate resampling is required; reassess during modelling if necessary

Key_Finding: Missing information is mainly represented using '?' rather than standard NaN values; several attributes have extremely high missingness
Implication: Convert '?' to proper missing values and choose suitable handling methods during preprocessing

Key_Finding: active and reopen_count contain only one unique value
Implication: Review for removal because constant features provide no discriminative information

Key_Finding: made_sla, sys_mod_count, u_priority_confirmation and notify show extremely limited variation
Implication: Review predictive usefulness before retaining these features

Key_Finding: caller_id, u_symptom, subcategory and location contain relatively large numbers of categories
Implication: Use suitable encoding and avoid uncontrolled dimensional expansion

Key_Finding: Many categorical attributes contain numerous low-frequency categories, especially caller_id
Implication: Consider rare-category grouping or alternative encoding where justified

Key_Finding: Category, subcategory and location show noticeable differences in reassignment rates
Implication: These attributes may provide useful predictive information

Key_Finding: Higher priority and urgency levels show higher observed reassignment rates
Implication: Priority and urgency appear potentially useful for predicting reassignment risk

Key_Finding: Opening hour, day of week, weekend status and working-hours status show differences in incident behaviour
Implication: Consider temporal feature engineering during preprocessing

Key_Finding: Incident activity is heavily concentrated in March-May 2016, with much lower monthly counts afterwards
Implication: Consider a time-aware validation strategy and interpret low-volume periods cautiously

Key_Finding: Five non-zero sys_mod_count observations are flagged by the IQR method because the feature is almost entirely zero
Implication: Do not automatically remove the observations; verify whether they are valid rare cases

Key_Finding: Several lifecycle-related attributes may contain information unavailable at initial prediction time
Implication: Perform final prediction-time availability checks before model training
